newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: New issues dominate pre-holiday Singapore shares.
newsitem.headline: New issues dominate pre-holiday Singapore shares.

text.p: New issues grabbed most of the interest and much of the volume on the Singapore stock market on Thursday as dealers prepared for a long weekend break.
Most Singapore markets are closed on Friday for a Moslem religious festival.
By the midday break at 0430 GMT, the benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) stood at 2,044.86 points, up 4.67.
"The index should benefit from book-squaring today ahead of the weekend," said one dealer.
Recent issues dominated the volume with new listings MMI Holdings and Raffles Medical Group, the two most active stocks.

Disk drive maker MMI Holdings, which debuted on Wednesday, rose six cents to S$0.60 on 17.9 million shares while healthcare company Raffles Medical Group, which began trading last week, rose 2.5 cents to S$0.565 on 7.7 million shares.

Shares in property and steel company Lion Teck Chiang began their first day of trading at Singapore $1.30 each, unchanged from their initial public offer. They rose to a high of S$1.38 but later slipped back to S$1.33 on 1.9 million shares.
Of the STII stocks, SembCorp rose 15 cents to S$6.45 while car retailer Cycle & Carriage fell 30 cents to S$14.90.
